messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGE: high-sev GPU OOM spike during prefill on cluster-serving-prod (us-west-2). 80% of requests hitting model-x-preload are failing with container restarts. Auto-escalation to oncall. Runbook: <https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-prefill-oom>.

tanner (oncall): ack, I'm on it. pulling logs now.

olivia (eng-runtime): pinging in. any customer-facing impact observed yet? metrics show 5xxs up from 00:03 UTC.

incident-bot: Alert details: sample failure rate 12% -> 18%, avg latency spike +200ms, node flaps on 3 hosts. dmesg snippets indicate OOM on GPU process (cuda driver) prior to container restart.

raj (sre-lead): Tanner — run `kubectl get pods -n serving -l app=model-x-preload -o wide` and paste pod names. We'll check node-level OOM logs.

tanner (oncall): pasted list: `model-x-preload-5f9c8`, `model-x-preload-6a2f1`, `model-x-preload-7b3d2`. Running `kubectl logs --previous` on 5f9c8 now.

olivia (eng-runtime): copying known mitigation steps: 1) enable prefill-token-trimming (fast) 2) route heavy-context requests to model-x-small variant 3) temporarily reduce batch_size to 1 on these nodes.

emily (cust-success): FYI I already have a ticket open for Org:AcmeCorp — they reported a large-context job failing ~00:10 UTC. Might be related. Please flag if we need to send a status update.

deploy-bot: `deploy-check` shows recent rollout of model-x v2.3 to serving-prod at 23:50 UTC yesterday. No config changes recorded for batching.

olivia (eng-runtime): Tanner — paste the tail of the crashing container log. Look for `CUDA_ERROR` or `out of memory`.

tanner (oncall): tail:
```
2026-03-14 00:11:02.132 INFO prefill: starting prefill for request id=abc123 tokens=18900
2026-03-14 00:11:02.400 ERROR runtime: GPU allocation failed: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY
2026-03-14 00:11:02.401 WARN kernel: Out of memory: Killed process 12456 (serve) total-vm:5120000kB
2026-03-14 00:11:02.410 INFO kubelet: Container exited with status 137
```

raj (sre-lead): status 137 = OOM kill. This matches node-level OOM. Which nodes? `kubectl describe pod` for owner node.

tanner (oncall): nodes: ip-10-0-44-12, ip-10-0-44-13, ip-10-0-44-14. All same instance type g4dn.xlarge (1 GPU). Node metrics show GPU memory pressure spikes.

olivia (eng-runtime): Hypothesis: long prefill tokens + batching created a combined allocation > GPU mem. We need an immediate mitigation: 1) disable prefill batching on these pods (set ENV PREFILL_BATCHING=false) 2) set MAX_PREFILL_TOKENS to 8192 via configmap for serving-prod 3) add routing rule to prefer model-x-small for contexts > 8k.

tanner (oncall): I'm applying a quick patch to the pod spec to set PREFILL_BATCHING=false on two crashing pods to test. Applying to `model-x-preload-5f9c8` and `6a2f1` now.

deploy-bot: Patch applied to 5f9c8 and 6a2f1. New pods restarting.

olivia (eng-runtime): Good. Also trigger KV cache eviction on the node to free memory: `curl -XPOST http://localhost:8080/evict-kv-cache` (on serving agent). Tanner can you run that via ssh?

tanner (oncall): evict request sent to ip-10-0-44-12 and 13. Response: `evicted 46MB`. Not huge but helpful.

emily (cust-success): Should we send a short customer note? There are ~12 active customers with heavy-context flows. Propose a brief status note: "We are investigating OOMs affecting long-context requests; routing to smaller model variants and mitigations underway." Thoughts?

raj (sre-lead): Yes send now. Keep it high-level and say estimated impact window ~30-45m while we roll mitigations.

emily (cust-success): sending now.

olivia (eng-runtime): Next checks: 1) confirm new pods come up stable for >2 min 2) monitor `nvidia-smi` on nodes for GPU memory 3) roll global config change if stable. Tanner, can you attach to one of the restarted pods and run a synthetic prefill with 10k tokens to validate?

tanner (oncall): attaching to 5f9c8-restart pod. Running synthetic: `python tests/synth_prefill.py --tokens 10000 --model model-x`

tanner (oncall): result: allocation refused but different log now — prefill was rejected with 422 (prefill too-large) after our env change. So mitigation blocked the request instead of causing OOM. :thumbsup:

olivia (eng-runtime): That's what we want: fail-fast and route to fallback. Start rolling the env change to other replicas in the pool, then update configmap MAX_PREFILL_TOKENS -> 8192 cluster-wide.

deploy-bot: Rolling update queued for label app=model-x-preload across serving-prod (12 pods). Staggering 2 at a time.

raj (sre-lead): Monitor for node flaps — if nodes continue rebooting, we may need to cordon and reprovision. For now mitigation is throttling prefill and routing fallback.

tanner (oncall): rolling applied to first 6 pods. Error rate dropping from 16% -> 6% over last 3 minutes.

emily (cust-success): customers notified: AcmeCorp, Dataify, BrightMaps. All acknowledged; AcmeCorp requested ETA if job in progress will be retried.

olivia (eng-runtime): For longer-term: add server-side OR policy to limit prefill allocations per-request and add a graceful trimming strategy that preserves last N tokens. Also add telemetry to detect >75% of GPU mem on prefill start.

raj (sre-lead): Agreed. Post-incident action items: 1) implement prefill admission control (owner: eng-runtime) 2) add node-level alert for sustained GPU mem >85% (owner: sre) 3) add runbook section for routing long-context to model-x-small (owner: product).

tanner (oncall): handing off to Raj for long tail — I've been on call ~2.2h. Leaving the channel. :wave:

raj (sre-lead): taking over. continuing monitoring and follow-up. Thanks Tanner.

olivia (eng-runtime): I'll open a PR for the config change and timeline for admission control.

emily (cust-success): will follow up with customers in 30m with update.

incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated (routing + fail-fast). Severity: SEV-2 -> monitoring. Channel remains open for follow-up and RCA. :eyes:

raj (sre-lead): tagging action items in #postmortems. Closing handoff.
